files.description: Bike-share trips, 1 September to 1 November 2025 (1500 rows): trip_id (whole number), rider_id (refers to riders.csv), start_station and end_station (refer to station_code in stations.csv), started_at (timestamp written as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM), duration_min (whole minutes; about 3% empty), distance_km (two decimals), fare (two decimals; about 3% empty), payment (card, app or cash; capital letters and spaces are inconsistent), rating (1-5 stars, whole number; about 19% empty).

task_text: In trips.csv, add a 10% peak-hour surcharge: for trips whose started_at time is from 07:00 up to 09:59, multiply fare by 1.1 and round to 2 decimals; other fares and empty fares stay as they are. `result` should be the total fare over all trips with a fare after the change, rounded to 2 decimals.
intended_computation: Read trips.csv; for trips whose started_at time of day is 07:00 to 09:59 multiply the fare by 1.1 and round that fare to 2 decimals (other and empty fares unchanged); return the sum of the non-empty fares after the change, rounded to 2 decimals.

acceptable_variants.notes: the reference rounds the floating-point product round(fare * 1.1, 2) per trip; about half of the fares end in 5 cents, so their exact product ends in half a cent and rounding half-even or half-up on the exact value may differ by 0.01 per such peak trip (intent writer flagged the per-trip rounding)
